Through the oval opening cut in the living wall, a sunlit birch understory stands pale and hazy beyond the sill where two stoppered flasks and a coil of dried twine catch the green-gold light coming back in across the counter edge.

Past the thick soft rim of the opening, a fern bank drips after rain in cool grey-green, its wet light washing in over the sill where a bundle of dried stalks leans in its cord and the nearest jar fogs faintly.
The gill-fleshed edge of the round opening frames a mossy stream beyond, its light skipping in small quick pieces that reach the floorboards just inside and slide across the knots in the grain.

A grove of other giant mushrooms stands beyond the sill in soft amber haze, their caps wide as rooftops and smaller than the tallest jar on the sill-ledge, their glow coming back in as warm amber pooled along the counter.

Through the opening, the foot of a vast root-buttressed oak fills the lower frame, roots as wide as the sill itself, hazed and secondary, their dappled light returning in and lying still across the nearest row of corked bottles.

Past the twine strung across the upper half of the opening, a bluebell drift under hazel hangs soft and violet-blue in the middle distance, its cool reflected colour faint on the pale undersides of the herb bunches dangling just inside.

A wet dark branch carrying one cluster of red berries rests just beyond the opening's soft edge, close enough to read clearly, and its thin wintry light comes in and catches the rim of a wide crock sitting on the sill.

The thick living wall makes a deep frame around the opening, and through it a clearing full of tall foxgloves stands purple and hazy, their light coming in as a faint rose wash across the light floorboards nearest the sill.

Beyond the sill, where a stone mortar and two small sealed pots stand in a row, the shoulder of another giant mushroom leans close, its pale underside visible through the opening and its soft reflected glow lying along the whole inner sill-ledge.

A river runs with faint interior light beyond the opening, visible between two trunks as a thread of cold silver smaller than the width of a cork, and that light comes in and makes the glass of every near jar briefly luminous.

Through the round opening, a slope of autumn beech fills the frame in full copper, soft and receding, and the warm orange it throws back in lights the edge of the counter and the bellies of the amber jars standing on it.

A soft grey wall of morning mist fills the opening, trunks fading into it at half their height, the whole view quieter and smaller than the room, and the mist-light comes in cold and even across the sill and the floorboards beyond.

Past the herb bunch knotted to the left edge of the opening, snow-laden spruce boughs press close in the near distance, blue-white and dense, and the bright reflected snow-light comes back in hard and clean across the inner sill and the row of pale stoppers.

Through the opening, a hollow lane of arching bramble curves away into soft darkness, framed by the gill-fleshed wall, and the single thread of light down its centre reaches in and draws a pale line across the nearest floorboard.

A whole hillside of glowing mushroom caps stands at dusk beyond the sill, dozens of them soft and amber-lit against the darkening slope, their combined glow coming in over the sill edge and warming the undersides of the jars standing there.

Beyond the opening, a still pool holds the sky in silver-grey, visible between two mossy trunks and smaller across than the widest jar on the sill, and its cold sky-light comes back in and lies flat and still on the counter surface.

A green-gold gap of afternoon light between two trunks fills the centre of the opening beyond the sill, and the light it sends back in is the warmest in the room, lying in a soft bar across the middle floorboards.

Fresh rain falls through the leaves beyond the opening, visible as a soft grey movement behind the sill where a covered crock and a folded square of mesh cloth sit, and the rain-light comes in cool and diffuse across everything inside.

A drift of luminous pollen crosses the clearing beyond the opening like slow gold snow, each particle faintly lit, and the gold it casts comes in over the sill and makes the dust on the nearest jar shimmer briefly.

A lantern-hung path curves away into the trees beyond the opening, the lanterns small and warm against the forest dark, and their orange light reaches in just far enough to touch the outer edge of the sill and the cork of the tallest bottle.

Through the opening's soft rim, a mushroom ring in deep moss stands beyond in the near middle distance, the caps low and even, and the green-shadowed light from the clearing inside the ring comes back in and falls cool across the inner sill.

A sky with two moons hangs beyond the opening in deep blue, both moons small against the dark and the nearer one about the width of a stoppered phial, their double light coming in and making twin pale shapes on the floorboards.

Past the twine and the three jars standing on the sill, a dark stand of holly fills the lower frame of the opening, its leaves catching winter light, and that sharp bright light comes back in and edges every jar on the sill in white.

A soft distant waterfall is visible beyond the opening as a pale vertical thread between dark trunks, smaller than the height of a corked bottle, and the cool mist-light it sends back in lies faint and even on the sill and the counter beyond.

Night trunks stand beyond the opening with luminous moss glowing faint green between them, the whole view dim and secondary behind the sill where a lit stub of candle makes the near jars glow amber, the outer light and the inner light meeting at the sill-edge.

Through the oval opening cut in the living wall, a sunlit birch understory stands soft and pale beyond, its green-gold shimmer coming back in across the sill where a corked amber phial and two small crocks catch it.

Past the crowded sill with its row of stoppered jars and the dried bunch hanging beside the opening, a fern bank drips after rain in soft grey-green, its cool diffuse light washing back along the counter edge just inside.

The thick gill-fleshed edge of the round opening frames a mossy stream beyond, its light skipping faint and small against the far stones, while a rippling bright reflection slides back in and moves slowly across the nearest shelf.

A grove of other giant mushrooms stands beyond the opening like a village of broad parasols, each cap hazed and smaller than the tallest jar on the sill, their amber undersides pulling warm light back in across the floorboards.

Through the opening, its lower edge worn smooth and holding three small bottles in a row, the foot of a vast root-buttressed oak stands dim and far, while one warm gap between its roots reaches in and lies along the boards.

Past the scrap of woven mesh across part of the opening and the little pot sitting below it, a clearing full of tall foxgloves stands pale and far, their pink softened by distance, their light returning faintly to the sill's edge.

Through the thick soft opening, its rim spored and pale, a wet dark branch carrying one cluster of red berries leans close in the frame, its faint cold light coming back in to catch the shoulder of a stoneware jar inside.

The gill-fleshed frame holds a hanging bunch of seedheads and two amber bottles on the sill; beyond, a slope of autumn beech spreads in full copper, hazed and warm, its bronze light flowing back across the counter and the nearest corks.

Through the opening, twine strung across its upper half holding a drying sprig, snow-laden spruce boughs press close and quiet beyond, their cold blue-white softened in the frame, their reflected brightness falling back in across the sill and the phials resting there.

Past the sill with its small row of crocks and a folded leaf pressed against the opening's edge, a hollow lane of arching bramble curves away into soft shadow, its filtered green light reaching back in to lie along the nearest shelf-edge.

The round opening frames a still pool beyond, smaller in the frame than the tall bottle standing on its sill, holding a pale reflection of sky, and that same sky-light comes back in faintly and rests on the stopper of the bottle.

A green-gold gap of afternoon light between two trunks shows through the opening, hazy and small, while the opening's sill — carrying a clay pot and a corked dark-glass bottle — holds that same warmth pooled around their bases inside.

Through the oval cut in the living wall, fresh rain falls through the leaves beyond in soft pale lines, its cool grey light coming back in across the sill where a row of small sealed jars sits quietly catching it.

A lantern-hung path curves away into soft dusk beyond the opening, the lanterns smaller than the cork of the nearest bottle on the sill, and their amber warmth comes back in to gild the sill's edge and the jar-tops resting there.

Past the bunch of dried stems hanging beside the opening and the two low phials on its sill, a mushroom ring lies in deep moss beyond, soft and circular and hazed, its pale reflected light returning to brighten the floorboards just inside.

Through the thick gill-fleshed frame, a drift of luminous pollen crosses the clearing beyond like slow gold snow, each mote smaller than a seed on the sill, and its soft golden light comes back in to warm the nearest row of jars.

The sill holds a stoneware crock and a tied bundle of dried leaves; beyond the opening, drifting cherry-blossom moves pale and slow across the frame, and its cool pink-white light returns inward, lying softly across the crock's rim and the bundle's knot.

Through the opening, its lower edge thick and spored, night trunks stand just visible in the frame with luminous moss glowing faint between them, and that cold green light comes back in to rest in a long stripe across the floorboards inside.

Past the scrap of mesh and the small amber bottle standing at the sill's corner, a wide fern meadow stretches beyond with seed-heads catching afternoon light, its warm haze returning through the opening to pool around the bottle's base and the sill's wood.

A dark stand of holly fills the lower frame of the opening, its leaves catching light that comes back in sharply bright across the sill's edge, where a squat corked jar and a folded paper packet sit lit along their near sides.

Through the oval opening, a soft distant waterfall falls into mist that rises back upward in the same column, hazy and small against the far treeline, its cool shifting light coming back in to move faintly across the nearest shelf of jars.

A hillside of glowing caps shows through the opening at dusk, each cap hazed and no taller in the frame than the large dark bottle standing on the sill, and their amber-rose light comes back in to warm the bottle's shoulder softly.

Through the opening's thick soft surround, a grove of other giant mushrooms stands in the middle distance like a village of pale parasols, hazed to near-white, and the strange diffuse light they shed comes back in and lies silver across the floorboards.

A twist of twine strung across the opening carries three drying heads of seed; beyond them, a clearing full of tall foxgloves stands soft and pink-purple in the frame, their light too faint to colour but enough to brighten the sill's pale wood.

The thick gill-flesh edge of the opening shows a slope of autumn beech in full copper beyond, small and glowing in the frame, and its warm amber light comes back in to lie in a soft band across the sill's row of corked bottles.

On the sill, a clay dish and a folded square of cloth sit before the opening where a soft grey wall of morning mist holds faint dark trunks fading into nothing, its pale even light returning to wash the whole near counter without shadow.

Through the oval cut in the living wall, snow-laden spruce boughs press close outside, white and muffled and small in the thick frame, and their cold bright light comes back in hard and clean across the sill, sharpening every cork and stopper.

A single dried leaf is tucked into the woven mesh across the lower opening; beyond it, a hollow lane of arching bramble curves away into dimness, and the green tunnel light it reflects comes back in softly and pools on the floorboard nearest the sill.

Past the sill where a tall dark bottle and two small crocks stand, a still pool holds the sky beyond, pale and mirror-flat in the frame, and the doubled light it throws returns in to catch the glass shoulders of the tall bottle.

Through the thick gill-flesh surround, a mushroom ring in deep moss stands in the clearing beyond, each cap rising no higher than the cork on the sill jar nearest the light, and the ring's pale reflected glow comes back in low across the floorboards.

Past the row of seven small jars standing on the sill, night trunks show beyond the opening with faint green luminous moss glowing between them, small and deep in the frame, and that cold green light returns in just enough to touch the nearest jar's base.

The woven mesh across the opening's lower half sags gently inward; beyond it, a wide fern meadow with seed-heads catching afternoon light stands soft and feathery in the frame, and the meadow's bright warm wash comes back in across the sill and the cloth laid there.

Through the oval opening, a dark stand of holly fills the frame, its leaves small and glossy-dim, and a shaft of white light driving through the gaps in it returns past the sill and strikes the side of a tall stoneware jar standing just inside.

Through the thick gill-flesh rim, a sky with two moons shows above the treeline in the upper part of the frame, one moon large and cream-coloured, one small and further, and their doubled silver light comes back in across the sill and the jars standing on it.

Past the gill-soft rim of the opening and the three small jars standing in a line on the sill, a bluebell drift under hazel shows hazy and blue-small in the frame, its cool reflected light washing the wall just inside the threshold.

Through the thick living edge of the opening, a clearing full of tall foxgloves stands in soft afternoon light, their spires no taller than a sealed jar seen against them from here, and the warm gap of light between the stems reaches back in and lies flat across the sill.

A tied bunch of grey-green lichen hangs beside the opening, and beyond the sill with its two phials a hollow lane of arching bramble curves away into shadow, the faint green light it filters coming back in to touch the nearest floorboards in a long pale stripe.

The round opening's soft edge frames a still pool holding the sky beyond, its surface hazy and bright in the middle distance, while the cold reflected light travels back in across the sill and the little row of stoppered vials standing on it.

Through the opening, snow-laden spruce boughs press close in the grey-white distance, their weight bowing them level with the cork of a dark bottle on the sill, and the blue-cold light they carry comes in across the counter and the nearest stoneware crocks.

Past the twine strung across the upper opening with its hanging dry-flower cluster, a mushroom ring sits in deep moss beyond, the caps small and pale against the green, and the diffuse light rising off the moss reaches back in to soften the shadows on the shelves inside.

Past the woven mesh half across the opening's lower edge and the stoneware pot on the sill, a river runs in the distance with a faint light of its own, soft and hazy in the frame, its cool glow coming back in to lie across the counter beside the nearest jar.

Through the oval opening, a soft distant waterfall falls into mist that rises back up to meet it, the whole thing hazy and small in the frame against the sealed crock on the sill, and the cool bright light it carries comes in across the sill boards and lies still on the nearest jar.
